chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from al-Qassim ibn Isma'il al-Anbari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibrahim ibn Mahzam, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

We mentioned the rulers of Banu al-Fulan (the Abbasids) before him, so he said: 'People perished because of their hastening of this matter. Indeed, Allah does not hasten on account of the haste of the servants. This matter has a limit/terminus to which it reaches. If it reaches that limit, they will not advance an hour nor delay an hour.'

key_terms.لم يستقدموا ساعة: They will not advance an hour
key_terms.لهذا الأمر: This matter (referring to the appearance of the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Abbasid rulers perish according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the Abbasid rulers as a case study for the spiritual peril of 'istijlal' (premature anticipation), warning that their hasty claims to authority stemmed from a misunderstanding of divine timing. He emphasizes that the Mahdi's reappearance is bound by a fixed, inevitable limit ('ghayah') set by God, meaning that human impatience cannot accelerate or delay the event, thereby validating the Shia doctrine of waiting for the specific signs rather than forcing a timeline.
